name: Cheung pessary trial
question: Does adding a vaginal pessary to pelvic floor exercise training improve symptoms and quality of life in women with symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse?

arms.label: Vaginal pessary plus pelvic floor exercise training

design.population: Women with symptomatic stage I–III pelvic organ prolapse.

verdictNote: Both prolapse symptom and impact scores improved more with pessary addition at 12 months.
takeaway: In women with symptomatic stage I–III prolapse, adding a vaginal pessary to pelvic floor exercise training improved prolapse symptom and impact scores more than pelvic floor exercise training alone at 12 months.

reports.label: 12-month primary report
reports.dateLocator: Europe PMC firstPublicationDate; PubMed print issue July 2016
reports.citation: Cheung RYK, Lee JHS, Lee LL, et al. "Vaginal Pessary in Women With Symptomatic Pelvic Organ Prolapse: A Randomized Controlled Trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2016;128(1):73-80. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000001489

results.measure: 12-month mean change in Pelvic Organ Prolapse Distress Inventory score; between-arm mean difference calculated from reported changes
results.note: Between-arm difference is arithmetic; prespecified alpha is not stated in the abstract.

results.endpoint: Prolapse impact on quality of life
results.measure: 12-month mean change in Pelvic Organ Prolapse Impact Questionnaire score; between-arm mean difference calculated from reported changes
results.note: Between-arm difference is arithmetic; prespecified alpha is not stated in the abstract.

harms.label: Overall complications
harms.note: The abstract describes rates as low and similar without event counts or types.
